world, and every one of them has to deterministically update on every player's device in a co-op session.You'll design that simulation module from the ground up as one of the first engineers on a new game team , working closely with the Engineering Team Lead and the Game Design department.Your responsibilities• Design and build a deterministic factory simulation that scales to hundreds of thousands of player-placed buildings• Own the sim architecture: data layout, tick model, threading, and serialisation format• Work with the Networking Engineer so the sim and co-op are designed together, not bolted on later• Set and meet the CPU performance budget for the sim on our minimum specification target• Review code and mentor other engineers on C++ and architectureAbout youYou will likely have:• Experience in professional C++ environments where you have architected, implemented, and maintained performant modules which are built on by other engineers, and lived with the consequences of your design choices• Deep knowledge of data-oriented design, multithreading, and performance, including CPU profiling and applying algorithmic complexity-based analysis to select the right data structures• Built a deterministic or lockstep system, or can show how you'd approach one• A track record of mentoring engineers and making architectural decisions in writing that others could follow and challengeIn addition, you may have:• 2+ shipped game titles• Worked on a factory, automation or simulation-heavy game• Worked in Unreal Engine, especially with Mass Entity or a custom ECS in UnrealIf you match most of this and the problem excites you, please apply.What we offer• Fully Remote: We employ directly inside Germany• Flexible working hours!• Paid overtime, on the rare occasions it happens• A hardware budget to ensure you have the ergonomic setup and hardware you need to work comfortably• A monthly personal growth allowance for courses, books or other learning material• Focus days to research or learn new skills• A yearly team gathering to meet and collaborate in person• A yearly salary review to keep your pay in line with the market, and an automatic increase of 2% per yearNext Steps & How to ApplyPlease apply via our recruitment agency 8bit via https://8bitplay.com/jobs/principal-c-engineer/• A one-hour technical conversation with the Engineering Team Lead about work you have done• A one-hour meeting with our HR and either our Founder/CEO or our Studio Producer, depending on availability, to assess shared values, how we will work together, and culture add• A second technical round in a format we pick together, based on what we need to assess for the specific role, taking no more than 2-3 hours of your time in total• A casual, unscored conversation with a group of people you'll be working with closely to learn more about us and for the team to learn more about you• An offer callWe give you a decision within a few working days of each stage, and we aim for the whole process from the first interview to an offer to take four weeks or less.For this role:• The first technical conversation covers systems you've built and how you
